evals.prompt: Define Playing to Win in 2-3 sentences. Include the five choices and explain why fit across choices matters.
expected_elements: Explains that the choices must reinforce one another

evals.prompt: Explain the mental model of the strategy cascade. Name at least 6 primitives and describe how they connect.
expected_elements: At least 6 of: aspiration, arena, customer, alternative, advantage, capabilities, systems, trade-offs, assumptions, fit checks

evals.prompt: Why does this skill exist for agents? Name the failure modes it prevents.
expected_elements: Prevents goal lists or initiative lists masquerading as strategy

evals.prompt: Distinguish Playing to Win from Five Forces, Seven Powers, OKRs, prioritization, and methodology. Give a mechanism-level reason each neighbor is different.
expected_elements: Seven Powers classifies durable moat sources
OKRs translate chosen strategy into objectives/results
Methodology designs process and verification gates
Playing to Win formulates integrated strategy choices

evals.prompt: List the ordered workflow taught by the skill, then identify which steps catch over-broad markets, slogan-level advantage, and missing operating discipline.
expected_elements: Operating discipline caught by management systems

evals.prompt: Give an analogy for Playing to Win that preserves integration across choices. Then name one bad analogy and explain what it gets wrong.
expected_elements: Uses an analogy with interlocking or mutually reinforcing parts
Maps the five choices to connected components
Explains that changing one choice changes the rest
Rejects a bad analogy that treats the cascade as independent boxes or a checklist

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: A B2B software company says it will win by selling to all finance teams with a simple AI dashboard. Apply Playing to Win by proposing a tighter cascade, labeling assumptions, and naming fit risks.
expected_elements: Narrows where-to-play beyond all finance teams
Names must-have capabilities tied to that mechanism
Labels assumptions rather than inventing certainty
Identifies at least one fit risk
